claim: Mice with compound epidermis-restricted BRAF/RAF1 ablation (Δ/Δep2) were born at Mendelian ratio but with their eyes open.
source: The mice (heretofore referred to as Δ/Δep2) were born at Mendelian ratio but with their eyes open (Figure 1B), probably as a result of the migration defects of RAF1-deficient keratinocytes (Ehrenreiter et al., 2005).
evidence: The manuscript directly states this observation about the birth phenotype of the mice, with reference to a figure showing the phenotype.

claim: The open eye phenotype in Δ/Δep2 mice is probably a result of migration defects of RAF1-deficient keratinocytes.
source: The mice (heretofore referred to as Δ/Δep2) were born at Mendelian ratio but with their eyes open (Figure 1B), probably as a result of the migration defects of RAF1-deficient keratinocytes (Ehrenreiter et al., 2005).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study (Ehrenreiter et al., 2005) to support this mechanistic explanation.

claim: Δ/Δep2 mice develop progressive skin disease symptoms including intense itching, scratching, partial alopecia, and self-inflicted wounds.
source: With time, however, they started to show symptoms of a progressive skin disease. These included intense itching and scratching resulting in partial alopecia and self-inflicted wounds (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript describes observed clinical symptoms and references Figure 1B showing the phenotype.

claim: Δ/Δep2 mice show epidermal thickening correlated with increased proliferation and expansion of both basal and suprabasal keratinocytes.
source: Histological examination of the non-affected areas revealed thickening of the epidermis correlated with increased proliferation and expansion of both the basal and suprabasal keratinocytes but not with keratinocyte apoptosis (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript reports histological findings with supporting figures.

claim: Epidermal thickening in Δ/Δep2 mice is not associated with keratinocyte apoptosis.
source: Histological examination of the non-affected areas revealed thickening of the epidermis correlated with increased proliferation and expansion of both the basal and suprabasal keratinocytes but not with keratinocyte apoptosis (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the absence of apoptosis with reference to supporting data.

claim: Filaggrin (FLG) expression in Δ/Δep2 mice is similar to that of controls.
source: Filaggrin (FLG) expression was similar to that of the controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to a figure.

claim: Δ/Δep2 mice show a rich dermal infiltrate comprised of activated mast cells, granulocytes, dendritic cells, and less abundant T cells and macrophages.
source: We also observed a rich dermal infiltrate comprised of activated (β1 Tryptase+) mast cells, granulocytes, dendritic cells and, less abundant, T cells and macrophages (Figure 1C–D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The manuscript describes the cellular composition of the dermal infiltrate with supporting figures.

claim: Δ/Δep2 epidermis shows robust expression of keratinocyte activation marker K6.
source: In line with the dermal inflammatory reaction, Δ/Δep2 epidermis was characterized by the robust expression of the keratinocyte activation marker K6, of the cell adhesion molecule ICAM1, and by the sporadic expression of MHC class II molecules (Figure 1E), all upregulated in inflammatory conditions including atopic dermatitis (Freedberg et al., 2001; Fan et al., 2003; Caughman et al., 1992).
evidence: The manuscript reports this observation with reference to a figure and cites literature on inflammatory conditions.

claim: Δ/Δep2 epidermis shows robust expression of cell adhesion molecule ICAM1.
source: In line with the dermal inflammatory reaction, Δ/Δep2 epidermis was characterized by the robust expression of the keratinocyte activation marker K6, of the cell adhesion molecule ICAM1, and by the sporadic expression of MHC class II molecules (Figure 1E), all upregulated in inflammatory conditions including atopic dermatitis (Freedberg et al., 2001; Fan et al., 2003; Caughman et al., 1992).
evidence: The manuscript reports this observation with reference to a figure and cites literature on inflammatory conditions.

claim: Δ/Δep2 epidermis shows sporadic expression of MHC class II molecules.
source: In line with the dermal inflammatory reaction, Δ/Δep2 epidermis was characterized by the robust expression of the keratinocyte activation marker K6, of the cell adhesion molecule ICAM1, and by the sporadic expression of MHC class II molecules (Figure 1E), all upregulated in inflammatory conditions including atopic dermatitis (Freedberg et al., 2001; Fan et al., 2003; Caughman et al., 1992).
evidence: The manuscript reports this observation with reference to a figure and cites literature on inflammatory conditions.

claim: K6, ICAM1, and MHC class II are upregulated in inflammatory conditions including atopic dermatitis.
source: In line with the dermal inflammatory reaction, Δ/Δep2 epidermis was characterized by the robust expression of the keratinocyte activation marker K6, of the cell adhesion molecule ICAM1, and by the sporadic expression of MHC class II molecules (Figure 1E), all upregulated in inflammatory conditions including atopic dermatitis (Freedberg et al., 2001; Fan et al., 2003; Caughman et al., 1992).
evidence: The manuscript cites three references to support this statement about inflammatory conditions.

claim: Δ/Δep2 mice fail to thrive.
source: Epidermal ablation of BRAF and RAF1 had profound systemic effects. The mice failed to thrive (Figure 2A) and presented with enlarged spleens and lymph nodes.
evidence: The manuscript reports this observation with reference to Figure 2A showing body weight data.

claim: Δ/Δep2 mice present with enlarged spleens and lymph nodes.
source: Epidermal ablation of BRAF and RAF1 had profound systemic effects. The mice failed to thrive (Figure 2A) and presented with enlarged spleens and lymph nodes.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this observation about systemic effects.

claim: Splenomegaly in Δ/Δep2 mice can largely be attributed to increased numbers of Mac1+Gr1+ cells.
source: The splenomegaly could largely be attributed to increased numbers of Mac1+Gr1+ cells (Figure 2B), a cell type found both in the spleen of a mouse model of FITC contact hypersensitivity/S. aureus infection and in the blood and skin infiltrates of atopic dermatitis patients (Skabytska et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 2B and cites a study on similar cell types.

claim: Mac1+Gr1+ cells are found in the spleen of a mouse model of FITC contact hypersensitivity/S. aureus infection and in the blood and skin infiltrates of atopic dermatitis patients.
source: The splenomegaly could largely be attributed to increased numbers of Mac1+Gr1+ cells (Figure 2B), a cell type found both in the spleen of a mouse model of FITC contact hypersensitivity/S. aureus infection and in the blood and skin infiltrates of atopic dermatitis patients (Skabytska et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites Skabytska et al., 2014 to support this statement about Mac1+Gr1+ cells.

claim: Lymph nodes in Δ/Δep2 mice contain elevated numbers of activated T, B, and dendritic cells.
source: The lymph nodes contained elevated numbers of activated T, B, and dendritic cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: Δ/Δep2 mice show leukocytosis in the blood.
source: In the blood, we observed leukocytosis and increased amounts of the chemokines CCL2 and CCL7, as well as of GCSF; in addition, serum IgEs were elevated in Δ/Δep2 mice (Figure 2D).
evidence: The manuscript reports this blood analysis finding with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: Δ/Δep2 mice show increased amounts of chemokines CCL2 and CCL7 in the blood.
source: In the blood, we observed leukocytosis and increased amounts of the chemokines CCL2 and CCL7, as well as of GCSF; in addition, serum IgEs were elevated in Δ/Δep2 mice (Figure 2D).
evidence: The manuscript reports this blood analysis finding with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: Δ/Δep2 mice show increased amounts of GCSF in the blood.
source: In the blood, we observed leukocytosis and increased amounts of the chemokines CCL2 and CCL7, as well as of GCSF; in addition, serum IgEs were elevated in Δ/Δep2 mice (Figure 2D).
evidence: The manuscript reports this blood analysis finding with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: Serum IgEs are elevated in Δ/Δep2 mice.
source: In the blood, we observed leukocytosis and increased amounts of the chemokines CCL2 and CCL7, as well as of GCSF; in addition, serum IgEs were elevated in Δ/Δep2 mice (Figure 2D).
evidence: The manuscript reports this serum analysis finding with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: The phenotype of adult Δ/Δep2 mice resembles a skin-specific allergic disease.
source: Thus, the phenotype of adult Δ/Δep2 mice resembled a skin-specific allergic disease.
evidence: The manuscript draws this conclusion based on the observed phenotypic characteristics.

claim: At 3 weeks of age, Δ/Δep2 mice do not groom more than control littermates nor show signs of skin rash except mild eyelid irritation.
source: To determine whether the systemic phenotype was secondary to the severe skin inflammation observed in adult animals, we examined Δ/Δep2 mice at weaning (3 weeks of age), at which stage they did not groom more than control littermates nor showed any signs of skin rash, except a mild eyelid irritation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript reports this observation with reference to a figure.

claim: Skin architecture and keratinocyte proliferation are not altered in 3-week-old Δ/Δep2 mice.
source: Skin architecture and keratinocyte proliferation were not altered at this stage (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to a figure.

claim: A 2-fold increase in mast cells is observed in 3-week-old Δ/Δep2 mice, but these cells are not activated.
source: In terms of dermal infiltrate, a 2-fold increase in mast cells could already be observed, but these cells were not activated (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to figures.

claim: Granulocyte and dendritic cell numbers are indistinguishable in 3-week-old F/F2 and Δ/Δep2 littermates.
source: Granulocytes and dendritic cell numbers were indistinguishable in 3 weeks old F/F2 and Δ/Δep2 littermates (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to a figure.

claim: ICAM1 expression is slightly upregulated in 3-week-old Δ/Δep2 epidermis.
source: In the epidermis, ICAM1 expression was slightly upregulated, while K6 and MHC II expression could not be detected (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to figures.

claim: K6 and MHC II expression could not be detected in 3-week-old Δ/Δep2 epidermis.
source: In the epidermis, ICAM1 expression was slightly upregulated, while K6 and MHC II expression could not be detected (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to figures.

claim: TSLP, CCL2, CCL7, and several cytokines (GMCSF, IL6, 4, 5, 13, 2) are significantly elevated in 3-week-old Δ/Δep2 epidermal lysates.
source: TSLP, CCL2, CCL7, and a number of cytokines (GMCSF, IL6, 4, 5, 13, 2) were already significantly elevated in the epidermal lysates, while only a trend could be observed for others (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The manuscript reports these measurements with reference to figures.

claim: Enlarged lymph nodes in 3-week-old Δ/Δep2 mice contain increased amounts of activated T, B, and dendritic cells.
source: Systemically, enlarged lymph nodes contained increased amounts of activated T, B, and dendritic cells, while the spleen was normal both in size and cell composition (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to figures.

claim: The spleen is normal in both size and cell composition in 3-week-old Δ/Δep2 mice.
source: Systemically, enlarged lymph nodes contained increased amounts of activated T, B, and dendritic cells, while the spleen was normal both in size and cell composition (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to figures.

claim: The number of monocytes and granulocytes is increased in the blood of 3-week-old Δ/Δep2 mice.
source: In the blood, the number of monocytes and granulocytes was increased, as were the levels of CCL2, CCL7, and GCSF. However, no significant difference in serum IgEs could be observed at this point (Figure 3D).
evidence: The manuscript reports this blood analysis finding with reference to Figure 3D.

claim: Levels of CCL2, CCL7, and GCSF are increased in the blood of 3-week-old Δ/Δep2 mice.
source: In the blood, the number of monocytes and granulocytes was increased, as were the levels of CCL2, CCL7, and GCSF. However, no significant difference in serum IgEs could be observed at this point (Figure 3D).
evidence: The manuscript reports this blood analysis finding with reference to Figure 3D.

claim: No significant difference in serum IgEs is observed in 3-week-old Δ/Δep2 mice.
source: In the blood, the number of monocytes and granulocytes was increased, as were the levels of CCL2, CCL7, and GCSF. However, no significant difference in serum IgEs could be observed at this point (Figure 3D).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 3D.

claim: The increase in T, B, and dendritic cells in lymph nodes and granulocytosis can be traced back to 10 days of age in Δ/Δep2 mice.
source: The increase in T, B, and dendritic cells in lymph nodes and the granulocytosis could be traced as far back as 10 days of age, at which time point GCSF was the only cytokine elevated in the serum of Δ/Δep2 mice (Figure 3E–F).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to figures.

claim: At 10 days of age, GCSF is the only cytokine elevated in the serum of Δ/Δep2 mice.
source: The increase in T, B, and dendritic cells in lymph nodes and the granulocytosis could be traced as far back as 10 days of age, at which time point GCSF was the only cytokine elevated in the serum of Δ/Δep2 mice (Figure 3E–F).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to figures.

claim: Ablation of both Braf and Raf1 in mouse epidermis does not directly disturb skin architecture but affects the cross-talk between keratinocytes and the innate and adaptive immune system.
source: Thus, ablation of both Braf and Raf1 in mouse epidermis does not directly disturb skin architecture but rather affects the cross-talk between keratinocytes and the innate and adaptive immune system.
evidence: The manuscript draws this conclusion based on the temporal progression of phenotypes observed.

claim: Δ/Δep2 embryos perform normally in an outside-in dye penetration assay.
source: Δ/Δep2 embryos performed normally in an outside-in dye penetration assay, indicating that stratum corneum permeability was not affected (Figure 4A).
evidence: The manuscript reports this experimental result with reference to Figure 4A.

claim: Stratum corneum permeability is not affected in Δ/Δep2 embryos.
source: Δ/Δep2 embryos performed normally in an outside-in dye penetration assay, indicating that stratum corneum permeability was not affected (Figure 4A).
evidence: The manuscript draws this conclusion from the dye penetration assay results.

claim: E18.5 Δ/Δep2 embryos lose three-fold the weight of littermate controls over 9 hours after birth.
source: We next monitored the weight of E18.5 embryos of different genotypes for 9 hr after birth as a proxy for transepidermal water loss and thus for the barrier function of tight junctions. Δ/Δep2 embryos lost three-fold the weight of littermate controls (Figure 4B).
evidence: The manuscript reports this experimental result with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: Reduced expression of E-cadherin (CDH1) is evident at P3 in Δ/Δep2 epidermis.
source: Molecularly, reduced expression of E-cadherin (CDH1), an adherens junction protein known to regulate tight junctions (Tunggal et al., 2005), and of the tight junction protein claudin 1 (CLDN1), which is crucial for the maintenance of the inside-outside barrier (Furuse et al., 2002) and has been found downregulated in atopic dermatitis patients (De Benedetto et al., 2011) was still evident at P3 in Δ/Δep2 epidermis, while occludin expression was normal (OCLN) (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 4C and cites literature on E-cadherin function.

claim: E-cadherin is an adherens junction protein known to regulate tight junctions.
source: Molecularly, reduced expression of E-cadherin (CDH1), an adherens junction protein known to regulate tight junctions (Tunggal et al., 2005), and of the tight junction protein claudin 1 (CLDN1), which is crucial for the maintenance of the inside-outside barrier (Furuse et al., 2002) and has been found downregulated in atopic dermatitis patients (De Benedetto et al., 2011) was still evident at P3 in Δ/Δep2 epidermis, while occludin expression was normal (OCLN) (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript cites Tunggal et al., 2005 to support this statement about E-cadherin function.

claim: Reduced expression of claudin 1 (CLDN1) is evident at P3 in Δ/Δep2 epidermis.
source: Molecularly, reduced expression of E-cadherin (CDH1), an adherens junction protein known to regulate tight junctions (Tunggal et al., 2005), and of the tight junction protein claudin 1 (CLDN1), which is crucial for the maintenance of the inside-outside barrier (Furuse et al., 2002) and has been found downregulated in atopic dermatitis patients (De Benedetto et al., 2011) was still evident at P3 in Δ/Δep2 epidermis, while occludin expression was normal (OCLN) (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 4C and cites literature on claudin 1 function.

claim: Claudin 1 is crucial for the maintenance of the inside-outside barrier.
source: Molecularly, reduced expression of E-cadherin (CDH1), an adherens junction protein known to regulate tight junctions (Tunggal et al., 2005), and of the tight junction protein claudin 1 (CLDN1), which is crucial for the maintenance of the inside-outside barrier (Furuse et al., 2002) and has been found downregulated in atopic dermatitis patients (De Benedetto et al., 2011) was still evident at P3 in Δ/Δep2 epidermis, while occludin expression was normal (OCLN) (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript cites Furuse et al., 2002 to support this statement about claudin 1 function.

claim: Claudin 1 has been found downregulated in atopic dermatitis patients.
source: Molecularly, reduced expression of E-cadherin (CDH1), an adherens junction protein known to regulate tight junctions (Tunggal et al., 2005), and of the tight junction protein claudin 1 (CLDN1), which is crucial for the maintenance of the inside-outside barrier (Furuse et al., 2002) and has been found downregulated in atopic dermatitis patients (De Benedetto et al., 2011) was still evident at P3 in Δ/Δep2 epidermis, while occludin expression was normal (OCLN) (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript cites De Benedetto et al., 2011 to support this statement about claudin 1 in atopic dermatitis.

claim: Occludin expression is normal at P3 in Δ/Δep2 epidermis.
source: Molecularly, reduced expression of E-cadherin (CDH1), an adherens junction protein known to regulate tight junctions (Tunggal et al., 2005), and of the tight junction protein claudin 1 (CLDN1), which is crucial for the maintenance of the inside-outside barrier (Furuse et al., 2002) and has been found downregulated in atopic dermatitis patients (De Benedetto et al., 2011) was still evident at P3 in Δ/Δep2 epidermis, while occludin expression was normal (OCLN) (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 4C.

claim: The architecture of P3 Δ/Δep2 skin is indistinguishable from that of controls.
source: The architecture of P3 Δ/Δep2 skin was indistinguishable from that of controls (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A); P3 epidermal lysates contained highly variable amounts of chemokines and cytokines, predominantly CCL2, IL6 and IL18.
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to a figure.

claim: P3 Δ/Δep2 epidermal lysates contain highly variable amounts of chemokines and cytokines, predominantly CCL2, IL6 and IL18.
source: The architecture of P3 Δ/Δep2 skin was indistinguishable from that of controls (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A); P3 epidermal lysates contained highly variable amounts of chemokines and cytokines, predominantly CCL2, IL6 and IL18. All were increased in the Δ/Δep2 epidermal lysates, albeit not significantly (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to a figure.

claim: The E-cadherin and claudin 1 downregulation is transient and no longer detectable in 3-week-old Δ/Δep2 mice.
source: The E-cadherin and claudin 1 downregulation was transient and was no longer detectable in 3 weeks old Δ/Δep2 mice (Figure 4D).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 4D.

claim: Single deletion of RAF1 (RAF1Δ/Δep) does not lead to increased body weight loss in E18.5 embryos.
source: Single deletion of RAF1 (RAF1Δ/Δep) and BRAF (BRAFΔ/Δep) did not lead to increased body weight loss in E18.5 embryos; consistently, the expression levels of tight junction proteins were normal in P3 epidermis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to a figure.

claim: Single deletion of BRAF (BRAFΔ/Δep) does not lead to increased body weight loss in E18.5 embryos.
source: Single deletion of RAF1 (RAF1Δ/Δep) and BRAF (BRAFΔ/Δep) did not lead to increased body weight loss in E18.5 embryos; consistently, the expression levels of tight junction proteins were normal in P3 epidermis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to a figure.

claim: Expression levels of tight junction proteins are normal in P3 epidermis of single RAF1 or BRAF deletion mice.
source: Single deletion of RAF1 (RAF1Δ/Δep) and BRAF (BRAFΔ/Δep) did not lead to increased body weight loss in E18.5 embryos; consistently, the expression levels of tight junction proteins were normal in P3 epidermis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to a figure.

claim: Δ/Δep2TX mice show conversion of both F to Δ alleles and strongly reduced expression of BRAF and RAF1 proteins in tail tissue.
source: These animals, termed Δ/Δep2TX, showed conversion of both F to Δ alleles and strongly reduced expression of BRAF and RAF1 proteins in tail tissue (Figure 5A).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: Δ/Δep2TX mice develop a milder disease than Δ/Δep2 mice, characterized by much slower kinetics (8 months between ablation and overt symptoms).
source: Δ/Δep2TX mice developed a milder disease than the Δ/Δep2 mice, characterized by much slower kinetics (8 months between ablation and overt symptoms), moderate keratinocyte hyperproliferation (assessed as increased epidermal thickness) and activation (as determined by K6 and ICAM1 expression), as well as by a modest increase in activated mast cells and granulocytes in the dermis (Figure 5B).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: Δ/Δep2TX mice show moderate keratinocyte hyperproliferation assessed as increased epidermal thickness.
source: Δ/Δep2TX mice developed a milder disease than the Δ/Δep2 mice, characterized by much slower kinetics (8 months between ablation and overt symptoms), moderate keratinocyte hyperproliferation (assessed as increased epidermal thickness) and activation (as determined by K6 and ICAM1 expression), as well as by a modest increase in activated mast cells and granulocytes in the dermis (Figure 5B).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: Δ/Δep2TX mice show keratinocyte activation as determined by K6 and ICAM1 expression.
source: Δ/Δep2TX mice developed a milder disease than the Δ/Δep2 mice, characterized by much slower kinetics (8 months between ablation and overt symptoms), moderate keratinocyte hyperproliferation (assessed as increased epidermal thickness) and activation (as determined by K6 and ICAM1 expression), as well as by a modest increase in activated mast cells and granulocytes in the dermis (Figure 5B).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: Δ/Δep2TX mice show a modest increase in activated mast cells and granulocytes in the dermis.
source: Δ/Δep2TX mice developed a milder disease than the Δ/Δep2 mice, characterized by much slower kinetics (8 months between ablation and overt symptoms), moderate keratinocyte hyperproliferation (assessed as increased epidermal thickness) and activation (as determined by K6 and ICAM1 expression), as well as by a modest increase in activated mast cells and granulocytes in the dermis (Figure 5B).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: Δ/Δep2TX mice show mild splenomegaly with an increase in Mac1+Gr1+ cells.
source: At the systemic level, we observed mild splenomegaly with an increase in Mac1+Gr1+ cells (Figure 5C) as well as enlarged lymph nodes containing activated lymphocytes and dendritic cells (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 5C.

claim: Δ/Δep2TX mice show enlarged lymph nodes containing activated lymphocytes and dendritic cells.
source: At the systemic level, we observed mild splenomegaly with an increase in Mac1+Gr1+ cells (Figure 5C) as well as enlarged lymph nodes containing activated lymphocytes and dendritic cells (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to figures.

claim: Increased numbers of lymphocytes and granulocytes are found in the blood of Δ/Δep2TX mice.
source: Increased numbers of lymphocytes and granulocytes were found in the blood, while IgE levels were comparable to controls (Figure 5E).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 5E.

claim: IgE levels in Δ/Δep2TX mice are comparable to controls.
source: Increased numbers of lymphocytes and granulocytes were found in the blood, while IgE levels were comparable to controls (Figure 5E).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 5E.

claim: Circumventing the transient barrier defect of Δ/Δep2 animals postponed and attenuated the clinical manifestation of the disease.
source: Thus, circumventing the transient barrier defect of the Δ/Δep2 animals postponed and attenuated the clinical manifestation of the disease.
evidence: The manuscript draws this conclusion from the comparison of Δ/Δep2 and Δ/Δep2TX phenotypes.

claim: Decreased activation of ERK is observed in non-lesional epidermis of adult Δ/Δep2 mice.
source: We observed decreased activation of ERK and increased activation of JNK, assessed by the phosphorylation of both MAPK and their respective downstream targets pRSK and pJUN, in non-lesional epidermis of adult Δ/Δep2 and Δ/Δep2TX mice; in contrast, phosphorylation of the p38 target MAPKAPK2 was not affected (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to figures.

claim: Increased activation of JNK is observed in non-lesional epidermis of adult Δ/Δep2 mice.
source: We observed decreased activation of ERK and increased activation of JNK, assessed by the phosphorylation of both MAPK and their respective downstream targets pRSK and pJUN, in non-lesional epidermis of adult Δ/Δep2 and Δ/Δep2TX mice; in contrast, phosphorylation of the p38 target MAPKAPK2 was not affected (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to figures.

claim: Phosphorylation of the p38 target MAPKAPK2 is not affected in non-lesional epidermis of adult Δ/Δep2 mice.
source: We observed decreased activation of ERK and increased activation of JNK, assessed by the phosphorylation of both MAPK and their respective downstream targets pRSK and pJUN, in non-lesional epidermis of adult Δ/Δep2 and Δ/Δep2TX mice; in contrast, phosphorylation of the p38 target MAPKAPK2 was not affected (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to figures.

claim: Low ERK activation and increased phosphorylation of JNK (and, to a lower degree, p38) are observed in 3-week-old Δ/Δep2 epidermal lysates.
source: A more detailed analysis of 3 weeks old animals confirmed low ERK activation and increased phosphorylation of JNK (and, to a lower degree, p38) in Δ/Δep2 epidermal lysates (Figure 6C).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: The levels of dual specificity phosphatase DUSP1 and DUSP10 are low in Δ/Δep2 lysates.
source: Consistent with this phosphorylation pattern, the levels of the dual specificity phosphatase DUSP1 and DUSP10, negative regulators of the stress kinases (Patterson et al., 2009), were low in the Δ/Δep2 lysates.
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding and cites literature on DUSP function.

claim: DUSP1 and DUSP10 are negative regulators of stress kinases.
source: Consistent with this phosphorylation pattern, the levels of the dual specificity phosphatase DUSP1 and DUSP10, negative regulators of the stress kinases (Patterson et al., 2009), were low in the Δ/Δep2 lysates.
evidence: The manuscript cites Patterson et al., 2009 to support this statement about DUSP function.

claim: BRAFΔep lysates are characterized by reduced ERK phosphorylation only.
source: BRAFΔep lysates were characterized by reduced ERK phosphorylation only, while RAF1Δep lysates showed increased phosphorylation of all three MAPK.
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding from the analysis of single deletion mice.

claim: RAF1Δep lysates show increased phosphorylation of all three MAPK.
source: BRAFΔep lysates were characterized by reduced ERK phosphorylation only, while RAF1Δep lysates showed increased phosphorylation of all three MAPK.
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding from the analysis of single deletion mice.

claim: ICAM1 expression is detected only in Δ/Δep2 lysates among the genotypes tested.
source: The expression of ICAM1 as marker of inflammation was detected only in the Δ/Δep2 lysates, leading to the hypothesis that the combination of high JNK, low ERK activation is at the basis of the inflammatory phenotype of Δ/Δep2 animals (Figure 6C).
evidence: The manuscript reports this finding with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: The combination of high JNK and low ERK activation is at the basis of the inflammatory phenotype of Δ/Δep2 animals.
source: The expression of ICAM1 as marker of inflammation was detected only in the Δ/Δep2 lysates, leading to the hypothesis that the combination of high JNK, low ERK activation is at the basis of the inflammatory phenotype of Δ/Δep2 animals (Figure 6C).
evidence: The manuscript presents this as a hypothesis based on the observed data.

claim: MEK inhibitor (trametinib) efficiently reduces ERK phosphorylation in both control and RAF1Δep epidermal lysates.
source: MEKi efficiently reduced ERK phosphorylation and slightly increased JNK phosphorylation in both control and RAF1Δep epidermal lysates, but increased p38 phosphorylation was only observed in the RAF1Δep (Figure 7A).
evidence: The manuscript reports this experimental result with reference to Figure 7A.

claim: MEK inhibitor slightly increases JNK phosphorylation in both control and RAF1Δep epidermal lysates.
source: MEKi efficiently reduced ERK phosphorylation and slightly increased JNK phosphorylation in both control and RAF1Δep epidermal lysates, but increased p38 phosphorylation was only observed in the RAF1Δep (Figure 7A).
evidence: The manuscript reports this experimental result with reference to Figure 7A.

claim: MEK inhibitor increases p38 phosphorylation only in RAF1Δep epidermal lysates.
source: MEKi efficiently reduced ERK phosphorylation and slightly increased JNK phosphorylation in both control and RAF1Δep epidermal lysates, but increased p38 phosphorylation was only observed in the RAF1Δep (Figure 7A).
evidence: The manuscript reports this experimental result with reference to Figure 7A.

claim: MEK inhibitor reduces the expression of phosphatases DUSP1 and 10 and of CLDN1 in RAF1Δep epidermis only.
source: Consistently, MEKi reduced the expression of the phosphatases DUSP1 and 10 and of CLDN1 in RAF1Δep epidermis only (Figure 7A).
evidence: The manuscript reports this experimental result with reference to Figure 7A.

claim: Within a month, RAF1Δep animals treated with MEK inhibitor develop an inflammatory skin disease characterized by K6 and ICAM1 expression in the epidermis, activated dermal mast cells, and increased TSLP.
source: Within a month, the RAF1Δep animals developed an inflammatory skin disease characterized by K6 and ICAM1 expression in the epidermis, by the presence of activated dermal mast cells and by an increase in TSLP (Figure 7B).
evidence: The manuscript reports this experimental result with reference to Figure 7B.

claim: In control animals, MEK inhibitor treatment reduces GMCSF, IL5, IL2 and CCL4 significantly.
source: In control animals, inhibitor treatment did not affect, or reduced chemo- or cytokine amounts; GMCSF, IL5, IL2 and CCL4 were reduced significantly, and a trend could be observed for IL4, IL17, IL27, and CXCL1.
